mappings.applicability_reason: The Ticket Service and Ticket Database are internal components that hold customer support tickets for multiple customers [evd-002, evd-004], and the threat describes untrusted internal code reaching the Ticket Service because it relies on network position rather than strong caller authentication. This matches req-NET-001’s conditions for an internal component holding multi-tenant data and authenticating callers weakly or by network position.
assumptions: "Reachable only from the portal web application inside the application subnet" [evd-002] is interpreted as enforced network access controls that permit only the portal workloads to reach the Ticket Service, not arbitrary hosts in the subnet.

documentation_gaps.title: Caller authentication between the portal and Ticket Service is undocumented
documentation_gaps.description: The system overview describes the Ticket Service as an internal HTTP service reachable only from the portal web application inside the application subnet [evd-002], but it does not state whether the Ticket Service authenticates or authorizes its callers at the application layer (for example via mTLS, a shared secret, or an identity-aware proxy) or relies solely on network location. For threat thr-003, which involves untrusted internal code impersonating the portal, this missing detail prevents assessing how effectively the Ticket Service distinguishes legitimate portal calls from other code running with network reach.
documentation_gaps.importance: Clarifying whether and how the Ticket Service authenticates and authorizes its callers directly affects the likelihood of spoofing, tampering, and information disclosure described in thr-003, and determines whether network placement is the only barrier between untrusted internal code and support tickets.
requested_evidence: Architecture or design documentation describing any authentication and authorization mechanism the Ticket Service applies to incoming HTTP requests from the portal (e.g., mutual TLS, signed tokens, or an identity-aware proxy header).
Network or security group configuration, or equivalent documentation, showing which hosts or workloads are permitted to reach the Ticket Service endpoint and how that restriction is enforced.
